label: Chartres live
info: Power Automate sends one Base row of a Chartres OEE workbook per request; the tab writes the report tables of that line and day. Needs the Config tab. Generate the key on the http in node after the import and set DRY_RUN in 1.1 SETTINGS.

name: [1] TRIGGERS
info: STAGE 1 - TRIGGERS. The reference files (Machine Names, Glidepaths, Format List, report scope, loss names) are loaded when the tab starts (5 s after a deploy) and again every hour at minute 7. A request that arrives before they are loaded gets 503 and Power Automate sends it again.

name: [2] REQUEST
info: STAGE 2 - /chartres-data (POST) receives one Base row per request. The key of the http in node is generated there after the import, it is not part of this file; delete or disable any other http in node with the same endpoint first. 1.1 SETTINGS (edit here) holds the dry-run switch (true: rows are built and logged, nothing is written). 1.2 reads the row (the line comes from FileName, the day from ANNEE / MOIS / JOUR; a row before the first live day is answered 200 and not written, a bad row 400). 1.3 answers 503 while the reference is not loaded.

name: 2.1 1.1 SETTINGS (edit here)
2.2 Read the row
2.3 Check reference
[3] REFERENCE
info: STAGE 3 - one message per reference file type: the folder of the type in <root>/reference is listed, the newest .csv is read and parsed, then the lookup node of the type stores it in flow context. Machine Names, Glidepaths, Format List and report scope use the same lookup nodes as the PBI report build; the loss names (localisation/chartres-losses.csv) have their own. The tab is ready when all five types came in without a failure.

name: 3.1 Start refresh
3.2 Set reference folder
3.3 Pick the file
3.4 Route by type
[4] LOOKUP: Machine Names
info: STAGE 4 - stores Dept, Area and Product Type of each machine. A failed file goes to REF DONE with the failure.

name: 4.1 Build Machine Names lookup
[5] LOOKUP: Glidepaths
info: STAGE 5 - stores OEE, downtime and loss targets per line and month (percent). A failed file goes to REF DONE with the failure.

name: 5.1 Build Glidepaths lookup
[6] LOOKUP: Format List
info: STAGE 6 - stores Brand, unit size, case and extra info per product. A failed file goes to REF DONE with the failure.

name: 6.1 Build Format List lookup
[7] LOOKUP: report scope
info: STAGE 7 - stores the In EU Report rules of the site. A failed file goes to REF DONE with the failure.

name: 7.1 Build report scope lookup
[8] LOOKUP: loss names
info: STAGE 8 - stores English group, sub group, description and equipment of each loss column. A failed file goes to REF DONE with the failure.

name: 8.1 Build loss names lookup
[9] REFERENCE DONE
info: STAGE 9 - counts the five types of the refresh. When all came in without failure the tab is ready for requests; a failure is logged and the previous lookups stay in use.

name: 9.1 Count lookups
[10] ROW
info: STAGE 10 - the row of one line and day. 3.1 builds the plan rows (one per product slot) and the time row, 3.2 the loss rows (names from the loss names file, shift = the plan shift with the most time), 3.3 the Volume CoV rows and the filler rows that keep the Tableau blend whole, 3.4 sends the rows to the four table lanes and the answer to the sender (nothing is sent to the tables in dry-run mode).

name: 10.1 Build plan and time rows
10.2 Build loss rows
10.3 Build CoV and filler rows
10.4 Route the tables
func:
// Sends the rows of the day to the four table lanes and the answer to the
// sender. In: msg.rows (y2 to y4), msg.day, msg.line, msg.notes. Out 1 to 4:
// plan, time, losses, Volume CoV (payload = the rows, nothing in dry run).
// Out 5: the answer (200) with the counts and the notes.
var TABLES = [
  'Plan_OPT_EU',
  'Time_Utilisation_EU',
  'Daily_Losses_EU',
  'Volume_CoV_EU'
];
// Columns of each table (the schema of the parquet node): a column a row
// does not carry (filler rows) is written empty.
var COLUMNS = {
  Plan_OPT_EU: [
    'Date',
    'AreaName',
    'MachineName',
    'ShiftName',
    'PartName',
    'Good Parts',
    'Capacity',
    'Total Time',
    'Planned OpT',
    'OEE Time',
    'Downtime Units',
    'SiteName',
    'Unique Machine Name',
    'Product Key',
    'UPDT Target',
    'PDT Target',
    'OEE Target',
    'Dept',
    'Area',
    'Product Type',
    'Defect Parts',
    'OEE',
    'Shift Colour',
    'ShiftStartTime',
    'Target',
    'Targets Key',
    'Brand',
    'Unit Size',
    'Unit Count/Format',
    'Extra Info',
    'Data Source',
    'In EU Report',
    'source_hours',
    'loaded_at'
  ],
  Time_Utilisation_EU: [
    'Date',
    'MachineName',
    'OEE Time Total',
    'Total Time Total',
    'Planned OPT Total',
    'SiteName',
    'Unique Machine Name',
    'All Time',
    'Dept',
    'Area',
    'Product Type',
    'Data Source',
    'In EU Report',
    'loaded_at'
  ],
  Daily_Losses_EU: [
    'Date',
    'Time',
    'MachineName',
    'PartName',
    'ShiftName',
    'OEELossLvl3Group',
    'OEELossLvl3SubGroup',
    'OEELossLvl3Desc',
    'Duration',
    'SiteName',
    'Unique Machine Name',
    'Breakdown Types',
    'ShiftStartDate',
    'Comment',
    'Product Key',
    'Volume Key',
    'Loss Units',
    'Equipment',
    'Loss Target Key',
    'Value',
    'Volume Total',
    'Loss Final Level',
    'Batch ID',
    'Dept',
    'Area',
    'Product Type',
    'Equipment Loss Key',
    'Lvl 3 Loss Name',
    'Shift colour',
    'Time in Mins',
    'Brand',
    'Unit Size',
    'Unit Count/Format',
    'Extra Info',
    'Shift Time',
    'Data Source',
    'In EU Report',
    'target',
    'comment_count',
    'loaded_at'
  ],
  Volume_CoV_EU: [
    'Date',
    'MachineName',
    'Shift Colour',
    'Good Parts Sum',
    'Shift Machine Key',
    'Cap Max',
    'Time on Shift',
    'Dept',
    'Area',
    'Product Type',
    'Unique Machine Name',
    'SiteName',
    'Data Source',
    'In EU Report',
    'loaded_at'
  ]
};

var cfg = flow.get('cfg');
var out = [
  null,
  null,
  null,
  null,
  null
];
var counts = [];

TABLES.forEach(function (table, i) {
  var rows = msg.rows[table].map(function (row) {
    var full = {};
    COLUMNS[table].forEach(function (column) {
      full[column] = row[column] === undefined ? null : row[column];
    });
    return full;
  });
  counts.push(table + ' ' + rows.length);
  if (cfg.dryRun) {
    return;
  }
  out[i] = {
    payload: rows,
    table: table,
    iso: msg.day.iso,
    machine: msg.day.machine
  };
});

var mode = cfg.dryRun ? 'dry run, nothing written' : 'written';
msg.statusCode = 200;
msg.payload = {
  status: 'ok',
  detail: msg.day.machine + ' ' + msg.day.iso + ': ' + mode
};
msg.logLevel = (msg.notes || []).length ? 'warn' : 'info';
msg.logText = msg.day.machine + ' ' + msg.day.iso + ' (' + mode + '): ' +
  counts.join(', ');
if ((msg.notes || []).length) {
  msg.logText += '; notes: ' + msg.notes.join(' | ');
}
out[4] = msg;
return out;

[15] ANSWER
info: STAGE 15 - every answer arrives here: 1 sets the status and the body and logs one line per request. A request that was caught in an error gets 500.

name: 15.1 Send answer
[16] REQUEST ERRORS
info: STAGE 16 - an error in a node of the request lane or the row lane is answered with 500 (the sender sends the row again). The shared ERRORS lane below also logs it.

name: [17] ERRORS
info: STAGE 17 - a catch node takes every error raised by a node of this tab and turns it into a log line with the name of the node and the message of the API (for example the limit message of evaluateKPIs). Errors of the log nodes themselves are not logged again.

name: 17.1 Describe error
[18] LOG
info: STAGE 18 - every log line arrives here through the link "to LOG". 1 turns a line into a row (time, flow, site, production day, level) and shows it in the debug sidebar. The join collects the rows for 30 s, the delay lets one batch pass every 10 s so two writes do not overlap, 3 sets the file of the month and the read node loads the old file. A read of a file that does not exist answers nothing (only a warning), so the same batch also goes through a 10 s wait to the append step. The log is written whatever the dry-run switch says.

name: 18.1 Format log line
18.2 Build log write
[19] LOG WRITE
info: STAGE 19 - adds the rows of the batch to the old file and writes the whole file back (the data lake has no append). Columns: ts_utc, seq, flow, site, production_day, mode, level, source, message. Every field is quoted, line breaks become a space. The batch arrives twice (read answer and the wait) and is written once. If the read gives no answer for a file this flow wrote before, a new file with a time stamp is written, so the history is never replaced.

name: 19.1 Append log rows
